posts.name: sbtang
posts.cooked:
HI there,

 

Quick question from from a newbie.. When you run out of Villain or Environment cards to play, do you recycle the trash back into play?
posts.raw:
HI there,

 

Quick question from from a newbie.. When you run out of Villain or Environment cards to play, do you recycle the trash back into play?

posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked: You shuffle the trash and resume playing the deck.
posts.raw: You shuffle the trash and resume playing the deck.

posts.name: Reckless
posts.cooked: When you need to draw next.  If you have a full trash and a card isn't played from the deck yet, you don't shuffle the trash into the deck.
posts.raw: When you need to draw next.  If you have a full trash and a card isn't played from the deck yet, you don't shuffle the trash into the deck.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: Also, as far as I'm aware, you only shuffle when you need to draw. If you're told to discard from the deck and there is no deck (because it's all in the trash), you instead do nothing. Most likely to be relevant (in the case of the environment) when you're fighting Akash'Bhuta :).
posts.raw: Also, as far as I'm aware, you [i]only[/i] shuffle when you need to draw. If you're told to discard from the deck and there is no deck (because it's all in the trash), you instead do nothing. Most likely to be relevant (in the case of the environment) when you're fighting Akash'Bhuta :).

posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked: I'm pretty sure if something says to "discard" the top card of an empty deck, it forces a shuffle.  Discard, draw, and play all force a shuffle.  Only "reveal" does not.

posts.name: Koga
posts.cooked:
So does this overwrite the previous official ruling in the Silver Gulch thread? Here's a few quotes from that thread. Edited to avoid revealing too much about the environment.

TheJayMann:

If I'm not mistaken, I'm pretty sure that it was stated a discard doesn't cause an environment/villain deck resuffle, the discard is simply cancelled. Also, a trash is not resuffled unless a card is to be played (environment/villain) or a card is to be drawn (hero). A trash is not to be resuffled simply because the deck is empty. So, even if there were only one or two cards left when played, it would simply put all the cards in the trash.

But, since I've been told that discarding doesn't cause a resuffle, this isn't an issue.

Koga:

I've always played that discarding can cause a reshuffle. Haven't seen any official ruling that says you don't reshuffle if you need to discard and there is nothing left in the deck. With this environment depending on the answer, would be nice to get an official ruling.

Christopher:

You would only reshuffle when a card needs to be played and the deck is empty. That said, if people play it "wrong", they'll reshuffle and then discard, so that's not too huge of an issue.
